questions.stem: Are Integration and Interoperability interchangeable terms?
options: Yes, they describe exactly the same capability
Yes, but only in the medical domain
No, they work together but their nature and purpose are distinct
No, because interoperability is only about hardware
No, because integration is a legal term and interoperability is technical
questions.explanation: Many people assume the terms are interchangeable, but although they work together, their nature and purpose are quite different.

options: Connecting systems and exchanging data to fulfil a range of objectives
Understanding data without any need for translation
Encrypting data before it leaves a system
Archiving data from retired systems
Defining medical codes for hospitals
questions.explanation: Integration involves connecting systems and exchanging data to fulfil a range of objectives.

questions.stem: When data is shared between integrated systems, what is often required for the receiving party to understand it?
options: A new database licence
A regulatory approval
A full backup of the source
A change of hardware
Translation of the data
questions.explanation: When data is shared between systems it often requires translation to be understood by the receiving party, and such translations conflict with the essence of interoperability.

options: The ability to connect any two systems with a connector
The ability to understand data without the need for translation
The ability to store data in multiple formats
The ability to replicate data across locations
The ability to compress data for transmission
questions.explanation: Interoperability is the ability to understand data without the need for translation.

questions.stem: What signifies the presence of interoperability between two or more systems?
options: The systems share a single database
The systems are owned by the same company
The systems use the same programming language
The systems are linked and exchange data seamlessly without requiring translation for comprehension
The systems have been integrated using ETL
questions.explanation: When linked systems exchange data seamlessly without requiring translation for the receiving parties to understand it, interoperability is present.

questions.stem: What example from the medical domain illustrates interoperability?
options: Various hospitals can readily interpret key terms and codes in shared data, whereas an average individual may struggle
Hospitals store patient records on the same server
Doctors translate every record by hand before sharing it
Patients carry printed copies of their records between hospitals
Hospitals use a single vendor for all their software
questions.explanation: In the medical domain, different hospitals can readily interpret the key terms and codes in shared data, which an average person could not, showing interoperability.

questions.stem: How do the translations needed in system integration relate to interoperability?
options: They are the foundation of interoperability
They are required before interoperability can exist
They are a measure of high interoperability
They conflict with the essence of interoperability
They have no relationship to interoperability
questions.explanation: Even when integration succeeds, the translations it requires conflict with the essence of interoperability, which is understanding without translation.

questions.stem: What does the degree of interoperability attained directly influence?
options: The cost of data storage
The effectiveness of integration
The size of the datasets exchanged
The number of connectors needed
The choice of database vendor
questions.explanation: The degree of interoperability attained directly influences the effectiveness of integration.

questions.stem: What happens to integration outcomes as the level of interoperability rises?
options: They become less predictable
They become more expensive
They require more translation
They are unaffected
They become more favourable
questions.explanation: The higher the level of interoperability, the more favourable the outcomes of integrations will be.

questions.stem: Which statement about integration and interoperability is NOT correct?
options: Integration and interoperability work together
Integration connects systems and exchanges data
Interoperability requires every exchanged message to be translated
Higher interoperability improves integration outcomes
Interoperability means understanding data without translation
questions.explanation: Interoperability is precisely the ability to understand data without translation, so requiring translation of every message is the opposite of interoperability.
